name: Pulsed dye laser for stretch marks
lead: Pulsed dye laser (PDL) treatment for stretch marks (striae distensae) is an in-office procedure in which a laser emitting light absorbed by blood vessels is applied to early, red or purple stretch marks (striae rubra). People use it to make fresh marks on the abdomen, thighs, hips, chest or shoulders less visible, aiming for skin that looks more even and shows less colour contrast when bare or in fitted clothes.

Stretch marks form when the dermis is torn or stretched during pregnancy, growth spurts, or weight and muscle gain, and begin as reddish or purple lesions that later become pale and atrophic [2]. Wikipedia's article on stretch marks, citing a 2014 systematic review, states that no treatment has been clearly shown to be useful once marks have formed, and it does not specifically discuss pulsed dye laser [2].

Published trial registrations show that PDL continues to be studied, for example against carboxytherapy in red stretch marks in a small 20-person study registered in 2024, with no results listed in the registry entry [1].

Small clinical studies have looked at the approach. A 1996 controlled study of 585 nm PDL on 39 striae found improved appearance with all four protocols tested and histology showing elastin restored toward the level of adjacent skin [3], and a 2014 split-body trial found a PDL plus fractional CO2 combination more effective than CO2 alone for white stretch marks [4].

paras: Pulsed dye lasers emit short pulses of light that are preferentially absorbed by hemoglobin. Proponents therefore apply them to striae rubra, in which dilated blood vessels contribute to the red or purple colour, rather than to older white marks. The sources reviewed for this article do not describe device settings, and none are given here.

Dye lasers use an organic dye as the lasing medium and can be tuned across a broad wavelength range, which lets the beam be matched to the absorption of tissues such as hemoglobin or melanin; in dermatology they are used for port-wine stains and other vascular conditions, scars and skin tone [5].

Stretch marks are commonly attributed to mechanical stretching of the skin, with elevated cortisol and corticosteroid exposure proposed as contributing factors [2]. Marks begin reddish or purple and later lose pigment [2]. Treatments that have been tried include tretinoin and hyaluronic acid (reported effective on early marks in some studies), various lasers, carboxytherapy and micrografting, but Wikipedia summarises the overall evidence as lacking a clearly useful treatment [2].

A controlled study by McDaniel, Ash and Zukowski, published in Dermatologic Surgery in 1996, treated 39 striae in people aged 23 to 52 with a 585 nm flashlamp-pumped PDL using four protocols, each compared with an untreated stria in the same person. All protocols returned striae toward the look of normal skin, a 10 mm spot size at 3.0 J/cm2 performed best, profilometry showed reduced shadowing, and histology showed elastin restored toward normal 8 weeks after treatment [3].

A 2014 randomised split-body trial in Advanced Biomedical Research enrolled three women with 88 striae alba lesions and compared fractional CO2 laser alone with CO2 combined with 585 nm PDL. Lesion area, patient-rated improvement and dermatologist-rated improvement were higher with the combination, with the authors noting the tiny sample, short four-week follow-up and no histology; one patient had post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation in a CO2-only lesion [4].

A registered trial, NCT06591208, started in September 2024 and enrolling 20 participants, compares PDL with carboxytherapy in striae rubra; its registry status was listed as unknown and no results were available [1].

The procedure appears in skin and body-improvement discussions as an option for fresh stretch marks, usually alongside other treatments. No forum material was available for this entry, so community claims are not documented in detail.

card.summary: A vascular laser aimed at fresh red stretch marks; trials are small and results are not firmly established.
card.aka: PDL, vascular laser for striae rubra
card.note: Reviews cited by Wikipedia find no stretch-mark treatment clearly effective; PDL-specific data in the sources are sparse.

quick.overview:
Pulsed dye laser is an in-office treatment used on new red or purple stretch marks, where the laser targets the blood vessels that give the marks their colour.

Sources reviewed describe only a small registered trial comparing it with carboxytherapy; broader reviews cited by Wikipedia report no clearly effective stretch-mark treatment.
quick.mechanism: The laser light is absorbed by hemoglobin in the small vessels of early marks, which proponents say reduces the redness.
quick.risks: The sources reviewed give no safety data for this use. Laser procedures generally are performed by clinicians, and results for older white marks are described as more limited.

chain: Laser light absorbed by hemoglobin in the small vessels of early marks
Less visible stretch marks, with colour closer to surrounding skin
angle.text: PDL is aimed at the red phase of stretch marks, where vessels give the colour, so treated marks can blend in more with the surrounding skin. It is a clinic procedure performed by a dermatologist.
